name: Cloudflare Agents x402
summary: Official Cloudflare docs and Workers/Agents SDK helpers to charge or pay over the x402 HTTP 402 protocol, including paid MCP tools.
description: Vendor-affiliated listing (Cloudflare). Official docs at https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/tools/payments/x402/ (HTTP 200; the no-trailing-slash path 307s there and is not used). The page describes accepting and making machine-to-machine payments with x402 on Cloudflare Workers and the Agents SDK: a 402 PAYMENT-REQUIRED response, a client-signed PAYMENT-SIGNATURE retry, and a PAYMENT-RESPONSE after settlement. It documents charge-for-HTTP-content, charge-for-MCP-tools (paidTool), and paying from the Agents SDK (withX402Client) or coding tools. Examples use the public facilitator at https://x402.org/facilitator, operated by Coinbase; the docs say the facilitator does not hold funds and only verifies and broadcasts a pre-signed transaction. Supported exact/upto schemes and networks are listed on that page (including Base and base-sepolia for test USDC). This is real on-chain money on mainnets; no payment was sent and no 402 was settled. Cloudflare Workers usage is billed under Cloudflare's own plans (https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/, HTTP 200). Refund terms for Workers or on-chain transfers were not taken from a terms page in this pass. This is documentation and SDK guidance for the already-listed x402 protocol, not a second copy of the protocol itself. No signup or spend.

agent_access.notes: Official Cloudflare documentation for x402 on Workers and the Agents SDK. Example helpers (paidTool, withX402Client) were not run. Settling a 402 on a mainnet moves on-chain funds; no payment was made. Docs name https://x402.org/facilitator (Coinbase-operated) in examples; the facilitator does not hold funds. Workers usage is billed separately (official Workers pricing page). This entry does not set mcp_endpoint.
